title: Seahawks-Patriots Week 1: Super Bowl LX rematch by the numbers
completenessNotes: Public PFF article was accessible in full through indexed web retrieval; headline, key bullets and full matchup analysis were exhausted. No unsupported pick, price or conviction was inferred.
game: New England Patriots at Seattle Seahawks

newMaterial.detail: Both Seattle and New England generated pressure on more than 40% of pass-rushing snaps in 2025, while both Sam Darnold and Drake Maye graded materially worse under pressure than from clean pockets. Darnold graded 90.6 clean versus 53.1 under pressure; Maye 90.1 clean versus 46.5 under pressure. Maye also held the ball longer (3.1 seconds) and carried a deeper average target depth, increasing the leverage of Seattle's pressure on his efficiency and turnover risk.
newMaterial.implication: reinforces pressure as a central game mechanism and specifically elevates Seattle pass-rush leverage against Maye without constituting a side or prop recommendation

newMaterial.detail: PFF graded New England first and Seattle second in coverage in 2025. Seattle also owned the league's No. 1 rushing grade, while New England's run defense ranked 18th. Seattle exploited that run-defense weakness in Super Bowl LX, but Kenneth Walker III is now in Kansas City, making carryover of that advantage less certain with Zach Charbonnet and the current backfield.
newMaterial.implication: supports a defensive/pressure-heavy framing while preserving uncertainty about whether Seattle can recreate its prior rushing advantage without Walker
